title: Microsoft Teams: raise hand and speak on mic and camera in events with up to 100,000 attendees
summary: The briefing accurately separates the planned 100,000-attendee capability from today's documented limits and controls. Two minor qualifications remain: the events policy reference carries a preview notice, and the reactions how-to and cmdlet reference disagree about the parameter's value type.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to support attendees raising their hands in Teams events with up to 100,000 attendees.
claims.quote: In events this size, attendees can now raise their hand in Teams when they have a question.

claims.claim: The default on arrival for the planned raise-hand capability above 20,000 attendees is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams 100,000 raise hand default; read roadmap, feature comparison, Plan for Teams events and release notes. They describe plans or current limits, not the new capability's default.

claims.claim: No source states that this change modifies existing large events automatically.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams 100,000 raise hand default scheduling form; read roadmap, Plan for Teams events, feature comparison and release notes. No passage specifies migration of existing events.

claims.quote: You must be assigned the Global Administrator role to access the License Management section and manage all licensing capabilities in the Teams admin center.

claims.where: Scope: Admin roles; controls[3].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Teams Administrator has read-only access to the Teams admin center License Management section.
claims.quote: Users assigned the Teams Administrator role can access the License Management section in read-only mode and cannot create, modify, or remove license assignments or settings.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends Teams Events Services for events with more than 20,000 attendees.
claims.quote: We recommend using Teams Events Services for events with more than 20,000 attendees.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Add-on Licenses > Teams Events shows organiser pack assignments.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Add-on Licenses > Teams Events. ... If one or more organizers are assigned an attendee pack, you see a table

claims.claim: Assigning a larger attendee pack after scheduling does not automatically increase that event's capacity.
claims.quote: No. Event capacity isn't automatically updated when a larger capacity attendee pack is assigned. The organizer must manually update the event capacity in the event scheduling form.

claims.claim: The large-audience creation toggle is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... turn the Events optimized for a large audience toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled prevents organisers with the policy from creating large-audience events.
claims.quote: To prevent organizers with this policy from creating events optimized for large audiences, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled
claims.fix: Add to the existing governance notes: 'The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference still labels the policy as preview.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamseventspolicy, which says 'Note that this policy is currently still in preview.' This caveat also covers the attendance command.

claims.claim: The audience setting is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Who can attend events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... in the Who can attend events optimized for a large audience dropdown list, select one of the following

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess EveryoneInOrganizationAndGuests restricts attendance for large events created by organisers with the policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess EveryoneInOrganizationAndGuests

claims.claim: An existing organiser's attendee pack is changed at Teams admin center > Add-on Licenses > Teams Events > Licenses > Attendee pack.
claims.quote: go to Add-on Licenses > Teams Events. ... On the Licenses tab, in the Attendee pack column of the table, select the drop-down in the user's row, and then choose the pack size that you want.

claims.where: controls[3].api; Governance controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: POST /v1.0/users/{id}/assignLicense is the general Microsoft Graph user-licence assignment operation.
claims.quote: Add or remove licenses for the user ... POST /users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/assignLicense

claims.claim: The assignLicense request's addLicenses collection specifies licences to add.
claims.quote: addLicenses ... A collection of assignedLicense objects that specify the licenses to add.

claims.claim: The assignLicense request's removeLicenses collection identifies licences to remove by skuId.
claims.quote: removeLicenses | Guid collection | A collection of skuIds that identify the licenses to remove. Required. Can be an empty collection.

claims.claim: The reactions default is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting engagement > Reactions.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Meeting policies. ... Select the policy that you want to edit. ... Under Meeting engagement, turn the Reactions toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: The cited reactions how-to documents Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowMeetingReactions Disabled to set the default to Off.
claims.quote: To set the default value for meeting reactions to Off for organizers with the policy, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowMeetingReactions Disabled
claims.fix: Add to controls[4].note: 'The reactions how-to prints Disabled, but the Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference lists AllowMeetingReactions as Boolean; confirm the accepted value against the installed module before scripting.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsmeetingpolicy?view=teams-ps alongside the existing how-to.

claims.claim: The admin Reactions setting sets a default in organisers' Meeting options rather than enforcing a per-event value.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can use the Teams admin center or PowerShell to set the default value for reactions in your organizers' Meeting options.

claims.claim: Organisers can change the reactions setting for each meeting and event they create.
claims.quote: Organizers can change the setting for each meeting and event they create.

claims.claim: Learn's presentation guidance notes that turning reactions off disables hand raise.
claims.quote: If you choose to turn off reactions, remember that this option disables the hand-raise feature.

claims.claim: Turning the large-audience event creation setting off after scheduling prevents the affected organiser from running or starting the event.
claims.quote: If you change the value to Off after a user schedules an event, they can't run or start the event.
